items.fullDescription: In January 2026, murals of faceless female silhouettes in yoga poses were scratched around the genital area in the Indian city of Gwalior. The figures depicted no identifiable women; they were attacked anyway. In 2024, sexually explicit AI-generated deepfakes of Taylor Swift circulated widely online, demonstrating a very different but related form of image violation. Across a scratched public wall and a fabricated digital image, the same question emerges: what happens when an image of a woman becomes the surface upon which sexualisation, humiliation or punishment is performed? This special issue asks where, if anywhere, a woman’s image can be assumed to be safe.

items.fullDescription: About the book: Human machine interfacing can be as simple as pressing a button or as complex and entangled (also entangling) as inserting a brain chip into the skull. science fiction. Humans with implants, prosthetic and hybrid humans with electronic and mechanical extensions are yet another level are no longer science fiction. Yet, human-machine interfacing has started long before the invention of these technologies. Machines did communicate with us and tell us about themselves even before chatbots were invented. The clanking of a hammer on the anvil tells us that it is old and dull. The whistle of a microwave tells us that dinner is ready. The process of interfacing is not a one-way process.

items.fullDescription: When, in September 2026, a post declaring the actress Katrina Kaif "finished" following her return to public life after childbirth accumulated lakhs of views and comments, the disproportion between judgement and object became, itself, the more legible text. items.fullDescription: At many universities, learning communities foster connectedness and belonging among students. Learning communities are typically composed of cohorts of students taking aligned first-year classes, but they take many other forms as well. At their best, they promote the perspective that learning is a collective activity in which knowledge is constructed through relationships with peers, professors, and communities, bringing together diverse voices and interdisciplinary perspectives. They provide a welcoming environment that eases the transition to college and provides a foundation for a peer network of academic support (Schreiber & Valle, 2013).

items.fullDescription: Bad Infrastructure Studies The “infrastructural turn” in the humanities is marked by an earnest critical materialism that has provided a necessary toolkit for analyzing how infrastructures consolidate structures of power through the material of daily life (Berlant 2016). Infrastructure studies scholarship from the last two decades has solidified how academics study and write about “the politics and poetics of infrastructure” as generating “the ambient environment of everyday life” (Larkin 2013). In the face of this now-established discourse, this panel asks: what else can the environmental humanities do with infrastructure?

items.fullDescription: Postmigration: Identity, Belonging and Cultural Transformation in Contemporary Societies Migration has profoundly shaped the cultural, social and political landscapes of contemporary societies. However, migration should not be understood merely as a process of geographical movement or as an experience limited to those who have personally migrated. In increasingly diverse societies, migration has become a constitutive element of collective identities, cultural practices, social relations and public discourses. The concept of postmigration offers a critical perspective that moves beyond conventional distinctions between migrants and non-migrants, foregrounding the complex ways in which migration continues to shape societies across generations.

items.fullDescription: Over recent decades, decadence studies has moved beyond earlier identifications of decadence with the Western European literary and artistic canon of the fin de siècle . Recent scholarship has, for example, developed new critical approaches to decadence, from translation studies to affect and sensory studies to postcolonial theory; illuminated the global dimensions of decadence; traced its afterlives and new literary histories; and examined its significance across diverse artistic and sociocultural practices, from food and fashion to performance and popular media. Taken together, these efforts underline the continued resonance of decadence as a capacious and multifaceted phenomenon for thinking about the many faces of modernity.

items.fullDescription: Bringing affect theory back to its seventeenth-century literary and cultural contexts, this conference seeks to explore how this period’s literature represents different affects; how reader responses are shaped by affect; and how both these negotiations reflect broader social or scientific developments of the period. items.fullDescription: Every act of communication, interpretation, and representation is an act of framing. In literary analysis, a “frame” might define genre, direct narrative perspective, or position a text within a historical moment. In linguistics, frames organize semantic understanding, govern pragmatic interaction, and underpin metaphor. In translation and interpreting, frames are negotiated, shifted, and sometimes shattered in the movement between languages and cultures. They are the selective filters that highlight certain elements while relegating others to the background, the conceptual structures that allow us to categorize, interpret, and communicate complex realities.

items.fullDescription: In 2007, Director Anne Lewis documented Hispanic/Latinx Appalachian "workers who speak about their lives, work, disappointments, and hope." Since that time, a significant boom of Hispanic/Latinx individuals has gained further recognition in Appalachian culture and community. Bands such as Appalatin and Che Apalache have been formed, academic papers have been written on migration patterns and demographic analysis, and oral history narratives have been collected. The very presence of these individuals has been established in the physical, factual realm of nonfiction spaces. However, very little has been explored in terms of Hispanic Appalachian fiction.

items.fullDescription: Special Issue Rationale Artificial intelligence has arrived in education with the force of a paradigm shift. Adaptive tutors, generative writing assistants, automated assessment, personalized learning pathways -- the claims are sweeping and the investments enormous. Education ministries, platform companies, and philanthropic foundations are converging on a single proposition: AI will transform how human beings learn. What remains largely unasked is whether this transformation is sustainable , and what, precisely, we mean by that word when we apply it to learning itself.
